2015_082_062315mtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education packet for the regular meeting of June 23, 2015 pairs routine monthly financial reporting - two Pentamation check registers, April and May purchasing-card, ACH and wire reports, and May-YTD fund summaries - with the year's closing budget actions. The Board was asked to adopt a 2014-15 budget amendment appropriating $145,113,344 in the General Fund, a 2015-16 appropriations resolution of $137,945,141 carrying operating millage of 17.8795 non-homestead and 4.9918 homestead mills plus 4.70 mills for debt retirement, and a resolution placing an 18.3795-mill and 5.99-mill operating renewal on the November 3, 2015 ballot, estimated to raise $33,583,000 in calendar 2016.

**Meeting.** Troy School District, County of Oakland, Michigan - Board of Education regular meeting of June 23, 2015; packet pages 3 through 321. Budget-book pages carry a D R A F T watermark and are paginated Page N of 30.

**Budget book and presentation.** Two 2014-15 General Fund expenditure totals are printed: $139,494,218 (excluding a $5,619,126 operating subsidy line) and $145,113,344. Two 2015-16 General Fund revenue totals appear: $136,512,079 and $135,831,716, the latter showing $680,363 of transfers in separately. Fund equity as a share of 2015-16 expenditures is stated at 12.29%, at 12.3% on the chart, and targeted at 12%. Debt service is shown at $38,613,697 / $38,219,577 on slide 22 but $16,650,931 / $16,588,938 in the budget book. State-aid membership is a blended count of 12,560.00; other enrollment is headcount, not FTE.

General Fund encumbrances were $1,935,417 with $23,739,339 available (16.53%), and the year-to-date result was $(921,452). Debt service revenue includes $37,504,183 of bond refunding proceeds and expenditures include $38,260,739 of other expenditures for the refunding payoff.

**Disbursement reports.** The check register for accounting period 11/15, printed 05/13/2015, totals $20,063,388.55; the period 12/15 register, printed 06/17/2015, totals $6,839,242.13. April PCard: subtotal $127,340.61, credits $(2,535.72), total expenses $124,804.89. May PCard: $155,016.78, $(3,145.09), $151,871.69. ACH debits were $33,352.12 in April and $31,409.33 in May; wire transfers were $1,909,620.79 in April and $1,892,965.66 in May.

**Policy.** B-2000 Member Development Opportunities / B-2002 Compensation and Expenses sets Board compensation at $100 per annum; adopted January 16, 1979, revised March 17, 1998 and April 15, 2003.

**Personnel (7.A-7.E).** Jennifer Gottlieb is appointed Director of Student Growth, Equity & Assessment effective July 1, 2015 on a two-year probationary contract. Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky is rated highly effective, awarded a $5,000 bonus and a 3.5% base salary increase, with his contract extended through June 30, 2017. Rick West and Mark Dziatczak are extended to the same date, as are 32 named administrators. The Troy Educational Secretaries Association agreement for July 1, 2015 to June 30, 2016 was ratified June 22, 2015 with a 2% schedule improvement, two step movements, and a 3% off-schedule payment.

**Business (9.A-9.D).** A November 3, 2015 special-election millage renewal proposal; a 2014-15 budget amendment; 2015-16 appropriations of $137,945,141 General Fund, $7,795,216 Special Revenue, $16,588,938 Debt Service, $98,866,705 2014 Capital Projects and $0 Capital Maintenance; and a $99,128.00 roof assessment contract to WeatherTech Consulting Group, Inc.

**Other (11.A).** A 2014/2015 School Year in Review video presented by Dr. Machesky.
2015_082_062315mtg.verbose:
Troy School District, County of Oakland, Michigan - Board of Education packet for the regular meeting of June 23, 2015, spanning packet pages 3 through 321. Contents fall into three blocks: draft 2015-16 budget-book and presentation material, every budget page watermarked D R A F T; machine-printed financial reports from Pentamation Enterprises, Inc. (report ACCTPA21); and the action items - a policy excerpt, personnel items 7.A-7.E, business items 9.A-9.D and item 11.A.

**Budget book and presentation, including internal inconsistencies.** Two different 2014-15 General Fund expenditure totals are printed: $139,494,218 on budget-book pages 5 and 26, excluding a $5,619,126 operating subsidy line, and $145,113,344 on pages 7 and 8 and on all presentation slides. Two 2015-16 General Fund revenue totals appear: $136,512,079 in the presentation and page 4 summary, and $135,831,716 on pages 5 and 26, where $680,363 of transfers in is shown separately. Fund equity as a percentage of 2015-16 expenditures is given as 12.29% on the summary slide and 12.3% on the fund-balance chart, against a stated 12% target. Debt service appears at $38,613,697 of revenue and $38,219,577 of expenditure on presentation slide 22 but at $16,650,931 and $16,588,938 in the budget book; the Debt Service Funds summary page is headed BUDGETED ENDING FUND BALANCE JUNE 30, 2015 where every other fund says June 30, 2016, and the debt retirement schedule labels its last two rows 2025-27 and 2025-28. State-aid membership is a blended count of 12,560.00, while all other enrollment is reported as headcount rather than FTE. Policies cited include B-2002 (first reading May 5, second reading and adoption June 23), B-1210, B-1301, B-1401 and J-2012; statutes cited include PA 300 of 2012, PA 152, Section 624 of the Revised School Code, the Open Meetings Act (1976 PA 267), MCL 211.24e, 211.34, 211.34d and 380.1211(3), Article 9 Section 31 of the Michigan Constitution, and STC Bulletin 3 of 2015. Firms named include Yeo & Yeo P.C., Nova Environmental, SimplexGrinnell, ThermalNetics, Nagle Paving, Barton Malow, TMP, Clark Hill PLC and Sodexo.

**Summary Revenue and Expense Budget Reports, May YTD Fiscal Year 2015.** General Fund (funds 101, 120 and 122): revenue of $142,706,181 approved against $114,213,845 actual, leaving $28,492,336 uncollected (19.97%); expenditures of $143,627,633 approved, $117,952,877 actual, $1,935,417 encumbered and $23,739,339 available (16.53%), including total instruction of $92,952,882 / $74,828,620 and total support services of $44,872,104 / $37,415,347; excess $(921,452); fund balance $21,380,015 at May 1, 2015 and $20,458,563 at May 31, 2015. Consolidated Special Revenue Funds (520, 529, 530, 535): revenue $8,635,670 / $7,557,189, expenditures $7,840,568 / $6,728,018, excess $795,102, balance $3,541,661 to $4,336,763. Food Service (520): $3,486,189 / $3,260,999 and $3,048,117 / $2,982,790, including $244,008 of capital outlay against no budget; excess $438,072; balance $1,320,716 to $1,758,788. Troy Career Center (529), entirely federally funded: $2,783,481 / $1,400,005 (49.70% uncollected) and $2,783,481 / $1,767,565; balance unchanged at $1,973,956. Adult & Community Education (530): local revenue overcollected at $2,366,000 / $2,824,714, expenditures $2,008,970 / $1,976,989, excess $357,030, balance from $0 to $357,030. Facilities Rental (535): $71,470 collected against no budget, $676 spent, balance unchanged at $246,989. Consolidated Debt Service (306, 307, 312, 314): revenue $16,114,013 / $54,727,832, including property taxes of $16,377,989 and $37,504,183 of bond refunding proceeds; expenditures $16,444,718 / $54,663,895, including $10,600,000 principal, $4,958,818 interest, $38,260,739 of other expenditures for the refunding payoff and $844,338 of transfers; excess $(330,705); balance $853,935 to $523,230. Consolidated Capital Projects (499, 414): $10,818 of investment earnings and $15,392,214 spent with $3,288,089 encumbered, including $15,350,696 of capital outlay, against no loaded budget; balance unchanged at $51,620,195. Internal Service Fund (681): $24,000 / $36 revenue and $24,000 / $25,354 expenditure; balance unchanged at $25,318.

**Check registers.** The register run 05/13/2015 covers accounting period 11/15 (selection transact.yr=15, period=10) and totals $20,063,388.55, with fund totals of $5,200,507.89 (101 General), $76,774.74 (120 Grant), $477,423.28 (122 Special Ed), $3,701,250.00 (306), $4,476,577.75 (312 2012 Refi), $4,162,225.00 (314 2014 Debt), $1,139,879.79 (414), $37,800.00 (499), $397,995.31 (520 Food Service), $86,975.21 (529 TCC Grant), $86,240.00 (530 Continuing Education), $218,958.67 (700 Student Activity) and $780.91 (701). Debt payments went to Bank of New York Mellon ($3,525,000.00 principal, $176,250.00 interest), U S Bank ($4,075,000.00 principal, $401,577.75 interest) and Huntington National ($3,000,000.00 principal, $1,162,100.00 interest, $125.00 fee). Other large items include the MESSA May 2015 premium of $954,380.07, MPSERS remittances of $876,957.79, $917,137.75 and $527,076.68, Blue Cross Blue Shield $144,056.24, Sodexo $345,809.55, Barton Malow $1,078,843.17 and Enviro Clean Services $254,771.42. The register run 06/17/2015 covers period 12/15 (cash account A1003) and totals $6,839,242.13, with $4,992,566.49 in fund 101, $33,949.56 in 120, $458,669.85 in 122, $750.00 in 306, $903,475.45 in 414, $1,850.00 in 499, $24,985.76 in 520, $38,542.12 in 529, $149,275.60 in 530, $188,957.59 in 700, $2,731.71 in 701 and $43,488.00 in 750 Memorial Scholarship. Notable payments include Enviro Clean Services $253,935.07, Barton Malow $804,833.82, the City of Troy $102,094.23 for salt pickup, CDW Government $53,088.00 for AirWatch and Edlio Inc. $24,000.00 for the district website.

**Purchasing-card, ACH and wire reports.** The April 2015 PCard report shows a subtotal of $127,340.61, credits of $(2,535.72) and total expenses of $124,804.89; the May 2015 report shows $155,016.78, $(3,145.09) and $151,871.69. ACH debits totaled $33,352.12 in April (Consumers $26,771.27, DTE $819.19, Heartland fees $5,272.45 and $489.21) and $31,409.33 in May (Consumers $17,171.66, DTE $14,048.42). Wire transfers totaled $1,909,620.79 in April, including payroll taxes of $776,589.96 and $752,862.79, and $1,892,965.66 in May, including payroll taxes of $755,930.03 and $770,396.04.

**Board policy.** B-2000 Member Development Opportunities and B-2002 Compensation and Expenses set Board member compensation at $100 per annum and allow reimbursement of actual and necessary expenses only where the Board approved the specific expense by majority vote at an open meeting beforehand or the expense fits an adopted category policy, with itemized statements filed with the assistant superintendent for business services. Adopted January 16, 1979; revised March 17, 1998 and April 15, 2003.

**Personnel items.** Item 7.A appoints Ms. Jennifer Gottlieb as Director of Student Growth, Equity & Assessment effective July 1, 2015 on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure; she returns from Macomb Intermediate School District, where she was Science Consultant for two years, after two years as Science Coordinator with Birmingham Public Schools and fifteen years with Troy Schools (three as Science and Math Coordinator, twelve teaching science at Athens High School), with degrees from the University of Michigan (1989), Columbia University's Teachers College (1990) and Oakland University (Education Specialist, 2011). Item 7.B reports Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky's first-year evaluation as HIGHLY EFFECTIVE, crediting him with launching One Troy and negotiating all labor contracts; the Board authorized a $5,000 bonus and a 3.5% base salary increase and extended his contract from July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2017 without tenure. Item 7.C extends Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning, through June 30, 2017, the narrative describing the action inconsistently as one-year extensions and as two-year successor contracts, with current contracts said to expire June 30, 2016. Item 7.D extends 32 administrators through June 30, 2017 without tenure, subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook: Ryan Brinks, Lara Dixon, Remo Roncone, Joe Duda, Timothy Fulcher, Audra Melton, Joyce Brasington, Janice Brzezinski, Brian Canfield, Tammy DiPonio, Sarah Glasser, Matt Jansen, Stephanie Miller, Melanie Morey, David Pass, Jeremy Whan, Melissa Curth, Robert E. Dowd, Bettie A. Goss, Dan House, William Turner, Amy Buchanan, Jonathan Cross, Diane Kocenda, Anthony Morse, Kerry Birmingham, Rob Carson, Michael Jolly, Stephanie Maynard, Kris Young, John Schiesler and Shawna Veit. Item 7.E ratifies a one-year agreement with the Troy Educational Secretaries Association/MEA/NEA for July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2016, tentatively agreed June 18, 2015 and ratified June 22, 2015: a 2% across-the-board wage-schedule improvement, two step movements on the 21-step schedule, a 3% off-schedule payment for those not benefiting from step movement, elimination of the $100/$200 health insurance premium deductible payments in Appendix 16 of the 13/15 agreement, and elimination of the former 4% off-schedule payment.

**Business items.** Item 9.A approves an Operating Millage Proposal for a Special School Election on November 3, 2015, conducted by the Clerk of the County of Oakland and certified to the Election Coordinator on or before August 11, 2015 under Michigan Election Law (Public Act 116 of 1954). The ballot asks 18.3795 mills against all property except principal residences, with 18 mills the maximum allowable levy ($18.00 per $1,000 of taxable valuation), and 5.99 mills against principal residences ($5.99 per $1,000), both for nine years, 2016 to 2025 inclusive; 17.8795 of the 18.3795 mills and the 5.99 mills renew authority expiring December 31, 2015, while 0.1205 mills restores millage lost to the Michigan Constitution's required reduction. Estimated revenue is $33,583,000 during calendar 2016; Paula Fleming, Board Secretary, certifies the resolution. Item 9.B adopts the 2014-15 budget amendment: $145,113,344 General Fund, $8,406,495 Special Revenue, $54,664,295 Debt Service, $19,434,618 2014 Capital Projects and $101,800 Capital Maintenance. General Fund revenue is amended from $142,706,181 to $142,113,297 and expenditures from $143,627,633 to $145,113,344, moving the projected result from $(921,452) to $(3,000,047) and the June 30 fund balance from $20,458,563 to $18,379,968. Item 9.C adopts the 2015-16 appropriations: General Fund $137,945,141 (one resolved clause prints $140,945,141), Special Revenue $7,795,216, Debt Service $16,588,938, 2014 Capital Projects $98,866,705 and Capital Maintenance $0. General Fund revenue is $136,512,079 (local $35,198,639, state $90,070,344, federal $3,395,503, transfers and other $7,847,593) against a July 1, 2015 balance of $18,379,968 for $154,892,047 available, with total instruction $92,744,689, total support services $45,123,193 and community services $77,259. Millage rates approved are 17.8795 mills non-homestead, 10.9918 mills commercial personal property, 4.9918 mills homestead and industrial personal property, and 4.70 mills on all classes for debt retirement. Debt Service revenue is $16,650,931 against $11,660,000 of principal, $4,922,738 of interest and $6,200 of other expenses; the 2014 Capital Projects Fund anticipates $67,489,416 of bond proceeds and $97,377,710 of capital outlay; Capital Maintenance appropriates $0 against a $701,919 balance. Item 9.D awards Roof Assessment and Consulting Services, reviewed by Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations, and owner's representative Michelle Kerns, to WeatherTech Consulting Group, Inc. for $99,128.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Item 11.A closes with a 2014/2015 School Year in Review video.
